text: Mr. Arthur Henderson (Labourite, Burnley) asked for leave to move the adjournment to call attention to the action of the Home Secretary in curtailing freedom of discussion in international questions by refusing the entry of Messrs. Oudegeest and Fimmina.

label: text
text: The speaker refused to put the motion declaring that it was impossible for the Home Secretary to differentiate in the importance of the two gentlemen mentioned from others under the Aliens Restrictions Act.

label: text
text: Mr. J. Ramsay McDonald, the Labour leader, preceded the point, pointing out the importance of the Congress.

label: text
text: The Speaker adhered to his ruling and the matter dropped.

label: text
text: Subsequently Mr. Henderson asked for an explanation of the refusal to admit Mr. Oudegeest, Secretary of the International Federation of Trade Unions, and Mr. Fimmins, Secretary of the International Transport Workers' Federation, who were desirous of attending the International Labour Conference on emigration in London.

Mountainlake (N. J.), June 21.
The death has occurred here of Mrs. Kate Jordan Vermilye authoress and playwright, whose pen name was Kate Jordan.—
Reuter's American Service.

label: text
text: A remarkable "find" has occurred here, a score of ancient muzzle-loading cannon being unearthed alongside the foundations of the old Central Station during the work of laying the foundations of the new Chartered Bank at the corner of Union Street and Beach Street.

label: text
text: They were all heaped together and though rusted are in a fair state of preservation. One bears the initials "F.M." over the touch-hole and all bear the Tudor crown, which gives some idea of their antiquity.

label: text
text: These cannon vary in size from a tiny ornamented affair, with a three-inch orifice, to a weightier piece of ordinance suggestive of a trench mortar.

label: text
text: It is suggested that they originally belonged to the old British East India Company, but their history has not yet been established, and how they came to be where they were is a mystery.—"S. T. Press"

label: text
text: "Governor General Wood is very popular with the Filipinos," said General McRae, formerly in command of the Philippine department, in an interview to day. General McRae will take command of the ninth district corps on Wednesday.

label: text
text: "The governor is especially popular," said General McRae, "with the older Filipinos who know that he has given the islands prosperity, schools and good roads."

label: text
text: He went on to say that American sovereignty was essential to the peace of the Far East and that the Philippines were essential to the maintenance of American prestige in the Pacific.-United Press

label: text
text: Sir Austen Chamberlain, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, stated in the House of Commons, in reply to a question, that he had now received confirmation of the notification of Brazil's withdrawal from the League of Nations. He could only express "his sincere regret that the Brazilian Government was taking that step, and he hoped that it might yet reconsider its intention to cut itself adrift from this great and increasingly powerful international organisation to the success of which it had made great contributions in the past.

label: text
text: Sir Austen "Chamberlain added that, though he had no official information, he was afraid that the Spanish Government was going to take a similar step.—British Wireless Service.

The Wedding of Robert T. Bryan, Jr., and Gertrude Indell Barndt, a teacher in the Shanghai American School, took place on Friday evening at 7.30 o'clock at the Shanghai American School. Following the ceremony the couple left for Nanking.
Both Miss Barndt and Mr. Bryan are popular members of the Shanghai American community. Miss Barndt came to Shanghai two years ago from Yacama, Washington, where she taught school. Previous to that she attended school at Walla Walla, Washington, after which she taught two years in Honolulu. Mr. Bryan was born in China and, with the exception of the years he spent in college in America, he has lived in Shanghai. Since graduating from college he has practised law in this city. He has also written several widely-read books on China.

text: A very pretty wedding was celebrated at St. Andrew's Cathedral on Saturday, June 12, the contracting parties being Oswin Gerald. Struys and Sybil Viola Scott. The ceremony was conducted by the Rev. Mr. Shetcliffe. The bride, who was given away by her uncle, Dr. F. W. F. Her white satin train was caught up at both shoulders with orange blossom and lined with shell pink georgette. The Misses M. Struys and M. text: Miss E. Clarke who was flower girl, wore an old Victorian white satin frock with forget-me-nots. Master B. Clarke was page boy. Mr. E. Hagedorn performed the duties of bestman:

text: There was a large gathering of friends and relatives at 3 Tanglin Hill, the residence of Dr. Noel Clarke, after the service, and many beautiful presents were displayed.

The Mexican consul general, Arturo M. Elias, in a statement to-day charged that Monsignor Caruana, bishop of Porto Rico and the West Indies, and papal delegate to Mexico, declared himself "a protestant," when entering Mexico at the Nueva Laredo immigration gate last March. The prelate was subsequently expelled by the Mexican government.
Monsignor Caruana denied the charges made by the consul general, branding them as entirely false. He said the signature to his declaration at Laredo was a forgery and that the Mexican inspector wrote the question and answers. Associated Press.

label: text
text: MIL TAFT SUFFERS FROM HEART TROUBLE.

label: text
text:
Washington, June 15.
Chief Justice. Taft who has been under the care of a heart specialist for more than a week was reported to-day to be progressing satisfactorily. Although he had planned to depart for his summer home in Canada last Friday, it is now expected that he will not leave before June 22. Upon the advice of his physician Chief Justice Taft decided to remain in bed several days longer. Associated Press.

label: text
text: Like Russia an outcry for the removal of the League from Geneva has broken out in the newspapers throughout Italy, which are angered by hostile demonstration's against the Fascist delegates and officials in Geneva.

label: text
text: The Popolo d'Italia, which is edited by Mussolini's brother; demands that the League headquarters be transferred to the Imperial Palace in Vienna, declaring that no Roman delegate can attend meetings in a city where public demonstrations against his country are "of daily occurrence.—Reuter.

text: SEEN AS SOURCE OF U. S. SUPPLY

label: text
text: The rubber Association of America has communicated with all leading consumers of raw rubber in the United States urging their cooperation in the establishment of American-owned rubber plantations in Sumatra.

label: text
text: A. L. Viles, the manager, said the entire scheme had been the subject of careful scientific and economic investigations. He said that the association planned no immediate action until assured of enough co-operation by manufacturers of rubber goods.

label: text
text: The Philippine Islands had been considered, he said, but it was his belief that the Sumatra project would most probably be accepted. He declined to estimate the amount of money necessary to carry out such an extensive development in the Philippines or in Sumatra. In another quarter it was learned that the association has planned tentatively to spend $50,000,000.

label: text
text: A project of this size and importance," said Viles, "must be thoroughly financed and a definite programme outlined before further steps can be taken. Prospects in the Philippines are still very unsettled because of the political and industrial condition existing to the investment of large sums of money there."—United Press.

label: text
text: Eugene A. Gilmore, Vice-Governor of Philippines, plans to sail from the United States for Manila on June 27 after spending some weeks at his home in Wisconsin.

label: text
text:
Before leaving Washington Mr. Gilmore had a farewell talk with President Coolidge. He told "The Associated Press" that several conferences with the President had convinced him that Mr. Coolidge is keenly interested in conditions in the Philippines and well informed concerning them.
The Vice-Governor recently completed recruiting forty-five teachers for the Islands, and on his way to the coast he planned to stop at various educational centres to continue his programme of interesting experts in the vocational and agricultural activities of the school system of the Philippines.

label: text
text: Mrs. Gilmore will remain in Wisconsin until their children have returned to school after the vacation and will join her husband in the Philippines next October.—Associated Press.

label: text
text: The bodies of three women, one man and one child were recovered late to day from the burned wreckage of a Union Pacific tourist sleeping car which burned early this morning at Cristal siding in Nevada. The origin of the flames is not known. Thirty people escaped injury by leaping from the windows when aroused from sleep. The sleeping car was part of the Continental Limited from Los Angeles to Salt Lake City. Associated Press.

label: text
text: Speaking at the half-yearly Budget meeting of the Government President Coolidge advocated a programme of "constructive economy" in Government expenditure by a means, inter alia, of a gradual reduction in the number of Government employees by refraining from replacing those dropping out.

label: text
text: He predicted that the current fiscal year would close with a surplus of $180,000,000 and the following year with a surplus of $20,000,000.

label: text
text: The President declined to promise a further reduction of taxes on the ground that it would be unfortunate to raise such hopes until the state of the Government's finances justified it.—Router's American Service.

label: text
text: Replying in the House of Commons to Mr. J. Ramsay MacDonald, the Labour Leader, Sir Austen Chamberlain said that both the Turkish National Assembly and Irak had authorised the ratification of the Turkish Treaty regarding Mosul forthwith, and it was eminently desirable that the British ratification should be given at the earliest possible moment. Unless, therefore, Mr. MacDonald expressed a desire for discussion on the Treaty. His Majesty would be advised to ratify it in a few days' time.—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: MUST BE ADMITTED TO TO LEAGUE.

label: text
text: Chancellor Marx told the United Press in an interview that Russia must be admitted to the League of Nations and be allowed to resume her normal international status, or the world be plunged once more into a devastating war.

label: text
text: "One of the most fundamental facts in International relations" said Chancellor Marx "is that the powers must accept Russia once more into the family of nations if they hope for peace.

label: text
text: "Russia will not attempt to impose communism on the rest of the world but she is entitled to choose her own form of government and work out her own means of preserving law and order. Germany knew she had nothing to fear from Russian propaganda or she would never have signed the recent treaty of neutrality with the Soviet government."—United Press.

label: text
text:
Washington, June 17.
American diplomatic officials today emphatically denied that they were in any way involved, even indirectly, in the League of Nations controversy, resulting in Brazil's withdrawal from the league. Rumours involving the United States in Brazil's withdrawal were circulated in Geneva and Rio Janeiro.

label: text
text: Edwin V. Morgan, the American ambassador to Brazil, cabled the state department a denial of the story that he had congratulated President Bernardes upon Brazil's resignation from the league.—Associated Press.

label: text
text: Another old resident of the Far East retired from Singapore yesterday (June 11) and sailed for Australia en route for Home, in the person of Mr. W. A. Sims, J.P. Mr. Sils has just passed the age of fifty-one, and has spent twenty-six years out East, at first in Hongkong and latterly in Singapore. The manager of the Commercial Union Insurance Company, Mr. Sims also did underwriting. He has taken a large part in the life of the City, served a useful term as Municipal Commissioner, is a justice of the peace, and a prominent freemason. Mr. Sims has been president of the Tanglin Club, and the various Church organisations will miss him as he was a leading spirit in the foundation of St Andrew's Hospital, which he generously supported.
